items_missed: Set Agenda: No real agenda statement (what he'd cover + rough time) and no 'sound good?' confirmation before he dove into questions — he just said 'I'll jump into it, I'll try to make it quick.'

Probe: Never confirmed zip codes for origin or destination, never asked about narrow hallways/tight turns, and never asked the direct stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').
Pricing: No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000), Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee were never mentioned — three of the biggest differentiators skipped entirely.
Estimate: Didn't tie the gun safe / heavy garage items into how they affect the time estimate, and no walk-distance or equivalents comparison used.
Save Your Ass: Entire prep speech skipped — no 'prep = shorter move = lower bill' framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip.
Quote/Booking: Never closed with 'anything else before I let you go?' and never gave office hours or how to reach the team.
Bonus: No rapport-building or humor moment, and no insurance explanation (No Worries + 60 cent/lb baseline) — same gap as the Pricing section.
top_strength: Grant proactively volunteered the cheaper Sunday rate without being asked — 'just wanted to be transparent with you and let you know that is an option if you want to save a few dollars' — which is exactly the kind of budget-conscious, trust-building move that keeps a shopping customer engaged.
coaching_note: Grant runs a clean, efficient call — the no-hidden-fees pitch and the clock rules landed well, and volunteering the Sunday discount was a genuinely good instinct. But he gave away real money on this call: Save Your Ass was skipped completely, and Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee, and No Worries damage coverage never came up at all. Those are the differentiators that separate Einstein from a generic mover when the customer is shopping around, which this one explicitly is. Build a habit of hitting all three every single call, and close with a real 'anything else before I let you go?' instead of ending the call as soon as the logistics are settled.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm, casual language ('Gotcha,' 'Lovely,' 'Sounds like a plan'), repeated name use, and proactive transparency on pricing kept the customer comfortable throughout, though there was no standout rapport or humor moment.
